newsitem.title: INDIA: India metals demand seen reviving in May.
newsitem.headline: India metals demand seen reviving in May.

text.p: A revival in demand for non-ferrous metals is expected from May after a period of stagnation, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Industrial demand for non-ferrous metals, especially copper, should pick up from May," said Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
Parikh said industrial users built up inventories ahead of a 10-day nationwide strike by truck operators.
"These inventories are getting over and industrial users will be back in the market placing orders," Parikh said.
Most government companies and agencies are also expected to book their orders in the new financial year 1997/98 (April/March) from May onwards.
"Funds will start flowing into the market," Parikh said.
Parikh said he would expect the state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) to revise its prices upwards in line with a recent surge in copper prices on the LME.
"We expect HCL to revise its prices upwards, though the LME prices of copper moved upwards and then steeply moved downwards," he said.
"We are a bit confused about the movement of LME copper prices," Parikh said.
India meets most of its non-ferrous metals requirements through imports and LME prices have a direct bearing on the local market.
In the week to Wednesday copper, tin and nickel made gains in line with LME prices.
Copper moved up by 150 rupees to 13,650 rupees per quintal, tin was up 300 rupees at 31,500 and nickel gained 400 to 36,500.
